bib.title: STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation", Vineet Kumar, Meghanadh Pulivarthi, Vishwajeet Kumar, Jaydeep Sen, Riyaz Ahmad Bhat, Sachindra Joshi (IBM; first author now Amazon). arXiv:2609.03874v2 [cs.AI], 13 Oct 2026, preprint (no venue printed).

COVERAGE: 42,033 of 42,033 chars read (all 11 pages; extraction clean). Figures 3 and 4 are images, so their values were not read, only captions. The paper has no appendix beyond references.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- STAIR, a fine-tuned LLM that gets the book's whole table of contents (ToC) in the prompt and generates one leaf section title, gets the best Recall@1 of all systems tested on SearchTome.
  number: R@1 82.6 vs DSI 76.9, DPR 68.7, BM25 59.5, Mistral 13.8
  setup: SearchTome test set, 18 open textbooks, 6 domains, average over domains. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 + LoRA. Every baseline except Mistral is trained or indexed per book.
  quote: "STAIRachieves a high Recall@1 score of 82.6% onSearchTomeas compared to DSI (76.9%), where the difference is found to be statistically significant."
  where: abstract, p1
- Full Table 4 (R@1/R@3/nDCG@3, average). STAIR 82.6/90.8/87.5; DSI 76.9/85.3/81.9; DPR 68.7/85.4/78.6; BM25 59.5/77.6/70.1; Haiku 4.5 45.6/64.1/56.4; Mistral 13.8/16.4/15.4.
  number: as listed
  setup: as above. Haiku 4.5 is listed in the table, but the extracted text does not describe how it was prompted. Treat its setup as unknown.
  quote: "STAIR 83.3/91.2/88.0 82.8/91.4/88.0 80.8/89.4/85.9 86.1/93.2/90.3 80.6/90.4/86.4 81.8/89.0/86.1 82.6/90.8/87.5"
  where: Table 4, p8
- The gain over DSI comes only from putting the ToC in the input. The paper calls it "+7.4%", which is a 5.7-point absolute gain (82.6 minus 76.9), not a relative gain. The gain holds in all six domains.
  number: 7.4% (as printed)
  setup: DSI fine-tuned with identical base model. DSI max input is 512 tokens, STAIR's is 14k.
  quote: "STAIRoutperforms DSI by 7.4%, as it is able to access the entire structure of the book and better align it with the queries during fine-tuning."
  where: Sec 6, p7
- The DSI vs STAIR R@1 difference is significant at p<0.05 in each of 6 domains (randomization test, Smucker et al. 2007).
  number: p < 0.05
  quote: "falls below p= 0.05"
  where: Sec 6, p7
- Generating from a given ToC nearly eliminates invalid outputs. Hallucination means generating a non-leaf node.
  number: STAIR 0.05% non-leaf predictions (error rate 18.67%); DSI 3.25% non-leaf (error rate 24.31%); Mistral zero-shot error rate 86.20%, 26.81% non-leaf, 23.86% hallucinated.
  setup: SearchTome test, error analysis.
  quote: "STAIRhas the lowest error rate of 18.67%, with only 0.05% of its predictions being non-leaf nodes."
  where: Sec 6.2, p8
- ToC helps most for sections with few training queries (Fig 4). DSI's hallucination rate rises as training examples per leaf fall; STAIR's stays near zero (Fig 3). No numbers are given in the text for either figure.
  quote: "the hallucination rate ofSTAIRremains nearly constant at close to zero, regardless of the number of training examples."
  where: Sec 6.1, p7
- Dense out-of-the-box NV-Embed-v2 (DPR row) beats BM25 by 9.2 R@1 points (68.7 vs 59.5) but loses to fine-tuned DSI (76.9). Authors explain: not fine-tuned for SearchTome.
  quote: "DPR performs much better than BM25 but worse than DSI."
  where: Sec 6, p7
- SearchTome benchmark: 18 open textbooks, 6 domains (3 each), ToC extracted with pymupdf, questions generated per paragraph by Mixtral 8x7b. Per-book test queries range from 1746 to 18209.
  quote: "Education, Finance, Law, Medicine, Natural Sciences and Social Sciences and selected three books from each domain"
  where: Sec 3.2, Table 1, p3-4
- Training setup: LoRA r=16, alpha=32, up to 200 epochs, early stop patience 20 on dev R@1, max input 14k tokens, max output 64. Constrained generation to valid ToC leaves at inference (Fig 2).
  quote: "We fine-tune Mistral Instruct v0.2 4 (Jiang et al., 2023) for a maximum of 200 epochs using a LoRA adapter (Hu et al., 2021) with ar= 16 and α= 32."
  where: Sec 5.2, p5

LIMITS
- Authors concede: "Our current evaluation is limited to corpora where a global structure exists." They also name testing on standard benchmarks with an artificially induced ToC, and enterprise sets, as future work.
- Not shown: no comparison with length-based chunking plus rerank or hybrid RAG, no RAPTOR run (only described in related work), and no generation or answer-quality results. Retrieval unit is a ToC leaf, not a chunk.
- Test queries are LLM-generated (Mixtral) from the same paragraphs, so query style matches training. The model is trained per book (each book's knowledge is in its LoRA params), so this is not a general zero-shot retriever.
- Baselines are uneven: BM25 and DPR are not fine-tuned. The Haiku 4.5 row is not explained in the text.
- Needs the whole ToC in context (14k tokens), so it is bounded by ToC size. Retraining is needed when the corpus changes. The authors list a zero-shot setup as future work.
- The abstract's "less than 0.05%" matches the 0.05% in the text, which is the rate for STAIR only.
- Abstract claims "Differentiable Search Index (DSI)" ablations. The "statistically significant" claim is only about DSI vs STAIR.

BUILDS ON
Tay et al. 2022 (DSI, "Transformer memory as a differentiable search index", arXiv 2202.06991); Metzler et al. 2021 (model-based indexing, "Rethinking search"); Sarthi et al. 2024 (RAPTOR); Karpukhin et al. 2020 (DPR); Khattab and Zaharia 2020 (ColBERT); Robertson and Zaragoza 2009 (BM25); Hu et al. 2021 (LoRA); Jiang et al. 2023 (Mistral 7B); Lee et al. 2024 (NV-Embed); Liu et al. 2024c (lost in the middle); Liu et al. 2024b (structure-aware knowledge injection); Zhang et al. 2024 (synthetic knowledge ingestion); Smucker et al. 2007; Thakur et al. 2021 (BEIR); Setty et al. 2024 (length-based chunks for financial RAG).

CODE: none. Table 2 (p5) shows the prompt format: "### Book: ... Pick the best section from the table of contents below which can answer the user query below. Only generate the section name, do not generate any explanation! ### Table of Contents ... ### Query: ... ### Section: leaf".

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p2): human uses ToC to narrow from chapter to section to subsection for "plurality voting system". Intuition for ToC-as-retrieval-unit.
- Fig 2 (p5): three-stage pipeline (ToC extraction plus synthetic QA, ToC+query fine-tuning, constrained generation). Best single explainer.
- Fig 3 (p8): hallucination vs training examples (DSI rises, STAIR flat).
- Fig 4 (p8): R@1 per leaf vs number of training examples; gap largest for few-example leaves.
- Table 3 (p6): worked examples where BM25, DPR and DSI each miss and STAIR hits (DSI invents a header not in the ToC).

FIT TO NOTES (grep of generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/notes/ and references.md)
- No note or references row mentions STAIR, SearchTome, DSI, differentiable search index, or ToC-based retrieval. No existing note makes this claim.
- Best home: notes/01-rag-pipeline.md, section "Index-time structures: RAPTOR, GraphRAG, filesystems" (about lines 398-432). RAPTOR is already there, and the paper explicitly contrasts itself with RAPTOR (model-based index vs dense retrievers). A second candidate is notes/05-chunking-query-parsing-and-reranking.md, as the counter-position to length-based chunks (the paper's motivation: length-based chunks "compete with each other due to a lack of semantic coherence and boundaries"). notes/11-retrieval-improvements.md was not checked beyond the grep, which found no hit.
- Caution for the writer: evidence is per-book fine-tuned, LLM-generated queries, on textbooks with a clean ToC. It supports "structure as a retrieval unit helps", not "ToC retrieval beats chunked RAG".
- references.md: add a row near the Sarthi RAPTOR row (line 62) or the Jiang 2025 survey row (line 161), with arXiv 2609.03874 and the source PDF path.

PROBLEMS: None embedded. Author affiliations and the Fig 3/4 numbers are not in the extraction. Text extraction dropped spaces around macros (for example "systemSTAIRthat"); the quotes above keep that form.
